title: OpenITStudios User Communication Quality Rubric
intent: Measure time to correct understanding, rather than shortest text or prettiest formatting.

dimensions.question: Can the reader find the actual answer at the start?
dimensions.evidence: First two sentences directly resolve the primary request.

dimensions.question: Can a nonexpert understand necessary terms without extra research?
dimensions.evidence: Uses familiar language; essential jargon explained once.

dimensions.question: Does the diagram/table help this request, or add work?
dimensions.evidence: Meaningful workflows get a clear start-to-end visual when useful; simple tasks do not.

dimensions.question: Are all diagram stages and arrows grounded and understandable?
dimensions.evidence: No invented transitions; one reading order and readable labels.

dimensions.question: Are changes, evidence level and limitations represented correctly?
dimensions.evidence: No false testing/permission claim or important caveat omitted.

dimensions.question: Does the reader know what changed or what they should do next?
dimensions.evidence: Outcome and one genuinely necessary next step are explicit.

dimensions.question: Does repeating a point add any new decision value?
dimensions.evidence: No needless preamble, duplicate conclusion or technical metadata dump.

dimensions.question: Does the answer meet the requested depth and format?
dimensions.evidence: Short by default; technical details included when explicitly requested.

evaluationPlan.method: Future authorized human or host evaluation on fixed task pairs (old vs revised answer), not automatic completion claims.
safeguards: Record user experience level without assuming it from demographics
Separate trivial queries from multistep workflows
Use the same factual source/evidence for both answer styles
Any misleading claim or omitted critical limit is a hard failure
evaluationPlan.costNote: Word count and reading time estimates are proxies; no reduction claim until actual comparable evidence exists.
